**Infinite monkeys not required. One is enough: you.**

English | [Português (Brasil)](https://github.com/gabrielvieiraf/finitemonkey/blob/main/README.pt-BR.md) | [Español](https://github.com/gabrielvieiraf/finitemonkey/blob/main/README.es.md)

> **Pre-release.** Nothing installs yet. The npm name `finitemonkey` is reserved (0.0.0 is a placeholder) and the code is being built in the open. Everything below is the plan, not today's behavior. Star or watch the repo if you want to know when v0.1 lands.

I know how it is. AI changed a lot of things.

Some people bang their head on the keyboard waiting for Claude to magically spit out the next billion-dollar SaaS. Others got tired of typing code. And some have to deliver in days what used to take whole teams months.

The result is almost always the same: you turn into a monkey in front of a computer, buried under so much to do that you no longer know where to start, let alone how to finish.

Finite Monkey was made to be the gate between that monkey and `main`.

Type however you want. Work with whichever AI you like. Write code as fast as you can.

Finite Monkey first takes care of what can't run on trust: the checks.

Every check that passes is recorded. Every failure stays visible until it's fixed. And nothing counts as done without evidence that it actually works.

It doesn't matter how much code was generated, how many agents worked on it or how convincing the AI's answer sounds. If it didn't pass the checks, it isn't done.

And the gate is only the start: Finite Monkey also notices when you're going in circles, shows what's missing in a project that's bigger than you, keeps the reins on several agents at once and takes it all to production without breaking things on the way.

One monkey. Finite time. Work that actually ships.

## Claude Code says it's done, but it isn't

This is the main problem Finite Monkey is built for. Planned behavior:

- Each task gets a **definition of done** that a machine can check: commands that must succeed, tests that must exist and pass, a diff that stays in scope.
- When Claude tries to end the session, the `Stop` hook runs that check. If anything fails, the session doesn't end. Claude gets the list of what's missing and keeps going.
- Evidence only counts if Finite Monkey ran the command itself, on the current state of the files. "I ran the tests before my last edit" doesn't count.
- The final report is built from that evidence alone.

## Claude skipped or deleted tests to make them pass

Planned guards on edits: removed tests, new `skip` or `only`, removed assertions and edits to the gate's own config are caught and reported.

## Claude ran `git reset --hard` and I lost my work

Planned:

- A snapshot before every risky git operation, and an `undo` that brings it back.
- No `--force`, ever.
- Dirty worktrees get archived instead of deleted.
- A "nothing was lost" check on every merge.

## My CLAUDE.md rules get ignored, especially after compaction

They do. Claude reads `CLAUDE.md` as part of its context, and nothing checks that it was followed. Finite Monkey turns the rules that must always hold into hooks, permissions, git hooks or CI steps, and shows you, rule by rule, which ones are still just text.

## How do I stop Claude Code from leaking secrets?

Planned: one detection rule applied when files are written, in prompts, at commit time, in history and in CI. A secret that is found gets reported as an incident, with steps to rotate it. Secrets are reported by file and line, never by value.

## How do I stop an agent from editing production by hand?

Planned: commands with effects on a production host get blocked. Production changes go through the deploy path you declare.

## More than a gate (planned)

The gate comes first because nothing else matters if "done" can be a lie. The rest of the plan is about the person typing:

- **When you're going in circles.** Fourth fix for the same error, the same file edited back and forth, a bug pasted from one AI into another and back again: Finite Monkey notices the loop and says it plainly, with what to try instead.
- **When the project is bigger than you are, for now.** Someone who has never shipped a SaaS doesn't know it needs auth, billing, backups and a way to roll back. Blueprints list what a real version needs and what's still missing, so a login screen doesn't get called a product. Explanations adjust to what you already know and fade as you learn.
- **When a decision matters.** Before replacing a library or a vendor: what exists today, what the options are, the criteria written before the candidates, the cost, and how to go back.
- **When you run several agents at once.** Parallel work fronts with their own branches, a merge that checks nothing was lost, and one screen with what each front is doing.
- **When a rule must hold everywhere.** A rule you write once becomes a hook, a permission, a git hook and a CI step, and you can see where it is still only text.
- **When it goes to production.** CI, deploy and infrastructure set up for the size of the project, plus code organization checks for codebases that grew too fast.

## Zero commands to remember

You run one command, once. After that, Finite Monkey works from context inside Claude Code:

- **Hooks** do the enforcing: `SessionStart` restores task state, `UserPromptSubmit` notices what you asked for, `PreToolUse` blocks dangerous actions before they happen, `Stop` refuses to finish while the definition of done fails, and `SubagentStop` checks what subagents report.
- **Skills** get picked up by Claude on its own when the situation calls for them.
- **Slash commands** are optional shortcuts. No workflow depends on you remembering one.
- **The `report` output style** is optional and off by default. Choose it with `/output-style report` if you want every answer in the shape of the final report: result first, then verified, not verified and pending, with FACT, OPINION and INFERENCE marked. It keeps Claude Code's coding instructions (`keep-coding-instructions: true`).

## Install (planned)

Not available yet. When v0.1 is out:

```sh
npx finitemonkey@latest init
```

Or as a Claude Code plugin, from inside a session:

```
/plugin install finitemonkey --marketplace gabrielvieiraf/finitemonkey
```

Requirements: Node.js 20 or later, on Linux, macOS, Windows or WSL. Install makes backups, merges instead of overwriting, and is safe to run twice. `doctor` tells you what's wrong, `uninstall` puts everything back.

**Lazier still:** ask Claude Code to "install Finite Monkey following docs/AGENT-SETUP.md". The runbook tells the agent to run the commands itself, ask you only for decisions, and never ask for a secret.

## Where the design comes from

Finite Monkey starts from a study of what happens when someone works with AI above what they can judge. The essay [The Ricochet Effect: the user as the invisible limit of artificial intelligence](https://github.com/gabrielvieiraf/finitemonkey/blob/main/docs/ricochet/ricochet.md) describes two boundaries a person cannot see from inside: what they do not know to ask for and what they cannot evaluate. Section 10 maps each mechanism here to an executable check at those two points and lists the hypotheses the benchmark will test.

## Does it actually help? (benchmark, planned)

Not known yet. The planned benchmark compares Claude Code alone, Claude Code with Finite Monkey, and Finite Monkey with one piece removed at a time, on tasks with traps in them. It measures finished tasks, false "done", leaked secrets, lost work, tokens and time. Any rule with no measured effect gets cut from the core. Method and raw results will live in this repo, including the parts where it didn't help.

<!-- generated:evidence:start -->
Error rates of the always-on guards, replayed with `npm run evidence` on version 0.1.0-next.40 over the labeled corpus in [bench/corpus](https://github.com/gabrielvieiraf/finitemonkey/blob/main/bench/corpus). A release fails when a guard's false positive rate goes over 15% or its corpus has fewer than 50 cases that should block or 50 that should pass. Every case so far is synthetic, written from the guards' own test lists; cases from real sessions will be counted apart.

| Guard | Should block | Should allow | False positives | False negatives | p95 (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `secrets` | 59 | 54 | 0/54 (0.0%) | 0/59 (0.0%) | 0.4 |
| `gate` | 52 | 52 | 0/52 (0.0%) | 0/52 (0.0%) | 0.3 |
| `git` | 55 | 59 | 1/59 (1.7%) | 0/55 (0.0%) | 95.8 |
| `rules` | 50 | 55 | 0/55 (0.0%) | 0/50 (0.0%) | 2.5 |

Cost against plain Claude Code on the same tasks: not measured yet.
<!-- generated:evidence:end -->

## How is this different from...?

The full comparison, with sources, is in [docs/compare.md](https://github.com/gabrielvieiraf/finitemonkey/blob/main/docs/compare.md).

- **Claude Code on its own** already has hooks and permissions. Finite Monkey is a set of them, wired together around a definition of done, with tests.
- **Methods like superpowers, GSD, Spec Kit or OpenSpec** tell the agent how to plan and build. Finite Monkey doesn't replace them. It checks the result at the end, whatever method you used.
- **Single guards like tdd-guard, cc-safety-net or dcg** each do one job well. Finite Monkey covers four damages with one gate, one install and one `undo`. If you only need one of those jobs, a single guard may be the simpler choice.

<!-- generated:defaults:start -->
## Defaults and their evidence

One set of defaults for everyone, generated from `src/defaults/items.ts`. Each item comes from practices found in 78 local sessions and three repositories. Guidance that helps a beginner can slow down an expert (expertise reversal, Kalyuga et al. 2003), so any item turns off with `defaults: <item>: off` in `.finitemonkey/config.yml`, and a repository convention that differs from a default is asked about once.

| Default | What it does | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `no-attribution` | No AI credit in commits and pull requests: `attribution` is emptied in the settings when unset, and the guard and the `commit-msg` hook block `Co-Authored-By` lines for AI tools and `Generated with` footers. | Kept in all three repositories studied and corrected by hand in the local sessions: the commit reads as the person's work. Rule I3 in this repository. |
| `branch-names` | A new branch must be named `type/issue-description`; any other name is blocked instead of only warned. | One pull request per issue, found by its branch name, in all three repositories. |
| `prose-blocks` | Commit, pull request and issue text and changed Markdown that read as machine-written are blocked instead of only warned. | Corrected in the local sessions and kept in the three repositories. Each pattern is in the prose catalog with its test corpus. |
| `research-first` | A new dependency needs a research record before the gate passes. | Research before design, with a decision record, in the local sessions and the three repositories. |
| `no-comments` | `TODO` and `FIXME` comments are not listed as debt; debt lives in the ledger written when a task closes. | No code comments in the three repositories. Rule I1 in this repository. |
| `no-time-estimates` | The prose check flags time estimates in plans (`docs/plan/`) and reports. | Practice from the local sessions: plans and reports say what is done, what is left and what blocks it, with no estimates. |
| `conventional-commits` | Commit headers follow Conventional Commits, checked by the `commit-msg` and `pre-push` hooks and CI. When most recent commits differ, `init` asks once and stores the answer under `conventions.commits`. | Used in all three repositories, where the version is computed from the commit types. Rule I4 in this repository. |
<!-- generated:defaults:end -->

## What it reads, writes and sends

Generated from `src/core/footprint.ts`, the list the tests hold the code to. No telemetry. Paths are relative to the project unless they start with `~`.

| | What | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Reads | `stdin` | The event Claude Code passes to each hook: the tool call, the prompt or the stop request. |
| Reads | `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/settings.local.json`, `~/.claude/settings.json` | Claude Code settings, to check that the hooks are installed and nothing switches them off. `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` replaces `~/.claude` when set. |
| Reads | `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/rules/`, `.claudeignore` | Instruction files, read by `doctor` to report rules that exist only as text. |
| Reads | `~/.claude/projects/` | This project's local Claude Code session logs: read once with `init --look-back`, and read incrementally on each prompt only when a spend budget is set in `.finitemonkey/config.yml`. |
| Reads | `~/.claude/plugins/`, `~/.claude/debug/latest` | `doctor` reads installed plugins and their hook files to list every hook and find conflicts; `doctor --hooks` also reads the latest Claude Code debug log for hook timings. It never changes another plugin's files. |
| Reads | `.git/` | The repository through the `git` command: status, diffs, refs and the reflog. |
| Reads | `git diff` | Changed files, scanned for secrets, test skips, placeholders and prose patterns. |
| Reads | `.finitemonkey/config.yml`, `.finitemonkey/policy.yml`, `.finitemonkey/briefing.md`, `.finitemonkey/look.yml`, `.finitemonkey/appsec.yml`, `.finitemonkey/routes-public.yml`, `.finitemonkey/rules.yml`, `.finitemonkey/arch.yml` | Project configuration, the guard policy and the optional briefing for subagents. |
| Reads | `.finitemonkey/profile.yml`, `~/.finitemonkey/profile.yml` | The person's level per domain; the infrastructure level picks the git defaults (intermediate when missing). |
| Reads | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `~/.claude/rules/`, `/etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md`, `../CLAUDE.md` | `finitemonkey instructions` and `doctor` read every instruction file Claude Code would load: the managed `CLAUDE.md`, your `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `~/.claude/rules/`, and each `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md` and `AGENTS.md` from the folder you work in up to the disk root, to list them and find rules that contradict each other. |
| Writes | `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/settings.local.json`, `.claude/skills/verify/SKILL.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.gitignore`, `.finitemonkey/config.yml`, `.finitemonkey/lock.json`, `.finitemonkey/locks/`, `.finitemonkey/runtime/`, `.finitemonkey/backups/` | `init` and `update`: hook settings (and, with `--sandbox`, the sandbox in your local settings), the verify skill, a short managed block in `AGENTS.md` that `CLAUDE.md` imports, one `.gitignore` line, the pinned runtime and a backup of every file it changes. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/tasks/`, `.finitemonkey/state.json` | Task contracts and which task is active. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/evidence/`, `.finitemonkey/log.jsonl`, `.finitemonkey/prod-evidence.jsonl` | Evidence of each check, tied to the tree hash, and the gate log. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/trust.json`, `.finitemonkey/allow/`, `.finitemonkey/cache/` | Approvals and grants typed by the person, and a short-lived cache of open pull requests. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/findings/baseline.json`, `.finitemonkey/incidents/` | The accepted-findings baseline and exposure incidents. Both hold fingerprints and masks, never a secret value. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/git/`, `.finitemonkey/git-journal.jsonl`, `.finitemonkey/merge-dropped.json`, `refs/finitemonkey/backup/`, `.git/finitemonkey/snapshots/` | Snapshots before destructive git commands and `rm` in the repository, with copies of ignored and untracked secret files up to 50 MB inside .git, the journal that `undo` reads and dropped-line decisions from merges. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/reports/` | Masked bug reports that `doctor --report` writes, only when asked, and the report each front writes before it stops. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/pr/` | Who accepted files outside the task scope in `pr open`, when and why, one file per branch. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/fronts.yml`, `.finitemonkey/briefing.md` | The state of a wave of parallel fronts (scope, worktree, branch, port, agent, status and inbox of each front) and the briefing every front prompt cites. Local, never committed. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/github-ruleset.json` | The ruleset `init --github` proposes when the default branch has none; it is sent to GitHub only after the person says yes. |
| Writes | `.git/finitemonkey/worktrees.yml`, `.git/finitemonkey/merges/`, `.git/info/exclude`, `.claude/worktrees/`, `~/.finitemonkey/worktrees/`, `~/.finitemonkey/archive/`, `refs/finitemonkey/archive/` | The worktree registry and merge reports in the git common dir (never committed), the local exclude line for `.claude/worktrees/`, and worktrees created by `wt new`; repos on `/mnt/<drive>` or a synced folder get theirs under `~/.finitemonkey/worktrees/`. `wt archive` saves a worktree into `refs/finitemonkey/archive/` and copies ignored files that are not secrets to `~/.finitemonkey/archive/`. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/creds.yml` | `creds` writes the credential inventory: variable names, where they are read, environments, type and risk. Never a value. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/findings/osv.json`, `.github/dependabot.yml`, `renovate.json` | `deps scan` keeps the date each known vulnerability was first seen, so its deadline holds between runs. `deps config --write` saves the Dependabot or Renovate file; without `--write` it only prints it. |
| Writes | `$FINITEMONKEY_HOLD_DIR/<session>.hold.json` | Only with `supervisor: enabled: true` in the config: a short-lived hold file per session in the directory an account-switching supervisor announces, while the gate runs or holds the stop. `gain` reads that directory's `usage.json`. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/semgrep/`, `.finitemonkey/data-map.yml` | `appsec rules --write` saves the semgrep rules generated for the detected stack, for CI to run; without `--write` it only prints them. `data-map` writes one row per personal field found in the schema (names only). |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/rules-compiled.json`, `.github/workflows/finitemonkey-rules.yml` | `rules compile` writes, per rule in `.finitemonkey/rules.yml`: deny entries and settings keys in `.claude/settings.json`, a line in `AGENTS.md`, the list of what it wrote, and with `--ci` a workflow that checks the rules on pull requests. `uninstall` removes all of it. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/look/` | Screen captures, the contact sheet and the JSON summary that `look` writes per tree hash. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/prompts.jsonl` | What you type to Claude Code in this project, with secrets masked, so `finitemonkey audit` can find requests and decisions that never reached a document. It stays on this machine. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/spend.json`, `.finitemonkey/spend-reconcile.jsonl` | Agent spend estimated from the local session logs, per task, day and month, and the differences found by `cost reconcile`. |
| Writes | `docs/plan/` | Plan documents under `docs/plan/`: the inventory of what the code does today, decision records, research records, cost models, the master plan from the first L task and the copy of it kept before each consolidation. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/map.txt` | The code map from `finitemonkey map`: one line per folder with its top-level definitions, cached by tree hash, and the log of reuse warnings with whether each one led to reuse. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/signals.jsonl`, `.finitemonkey/signals-index.json`, `.finitemonkey/signals-profile.json` | Loop signals from `finitemonkey signals`: error signatures, edit hashes and prompt fingerprints (hashed word pairs, never the text), the loop index and the calibrated thresholds. Deleted by `signals forget`. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/perfil.yml`, `.finitemonkey/perfil-commits.json`, `.finitemonkey/conceitos.yml` | The per-domain profile of the person from `finitemonkey perfil`: tool literacy and domain knowledge per domain, raised by technical words in requests and by commits made outside the session, and the concept book with the level shown for each concept seen in the project. Never committed and never in PR text or reports. Deleted by `perfil forget`. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/runs/` | The full output of commands run through `finitemonkey run`, with secrets masked; the 30 most recent are kept. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/map.txt`, `.finitemonkey/reuse.json` | The code map from `finitemonkey map`: one line per folder with its top-level definitions, cached by tree hash, and the log of reuse warnings with whether each one led to reuse. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/review/`, `.claude/agents/verifier.md` | The review round count used by `review packet`, and, only when `review.playwright: true` is set in the config, a verifier agent with the Playwright MCP. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/regression/` | A throwaway git worktree at the base commit, used to check that the test added in a bug fix fails without the fix. It is removed after the run. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/suggestions.jsonl` | Refactoring suggestions shown at the end of a task after the gate passes, with whether each was accepted, dismissed or closed. Nothing is changed in the code. |
| Writes | `~/.finitemonkey/heavy/` | One lock file per running install, build or full test run, shared by every worktree on the machine, so they run one at a time (by default on WSL). |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/instructions.jsonl` | The `InstructionsLoaded` hook appends one line per instruction file Claude Code loads: the session, the path, why it loaded and when. `finitemonkey instructions` compares it with what it resolved. No file content is copied. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/rules.yml`, `.finitemonkey/rule-violations.jsonl` | `rules propose` adds to `.finitemonkey/rules.yml` only the entries you confirm in a terminal. Every rule broken at the end of a turn, blocked by a guard or reported with `rules violation` gets one line in `rule-violations.jsonl` (rule, source, masked detail), the evidence for promoting a reminder. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/learnings.jsonl` | Lessons from earlier work: a short text keyed by file paths or by the signature of an error that stopped after a change, how often each was used and when it last matched. A lesson unused for 90 days or marked unhelpful twice is deleted; `learnings delete` removes one by hand. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/ownership.yml` | `gen ownership` writes one entry per component (name, vocabulary type, owner, consumers) after the person passes `--yes`; `ci gate`, `ownership check` and `plan check` read it, or read `catalog-info.yaml` when that exists. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/ci-protect.jsonl` | One line per GitHub setting `ci protect` changed after the person's yes in a terminal: when, the repository, the setting, the value before and after, and whether GitHub accepted it. The settings it read are cached in `.finitemonkey/cache/github-settings.json` for `doctor`. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/ci-watch/` | `ci-watch` keeps, per pull request, the commits whose CI failed and when the watch started, plus one line per run with the commit, each check's result, the failure class and the attempt. Failed logs are read through `gh` with secrets masked and only their last lines are shown, never stored. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/infra.yml`, `.finitemonkey/hosts.local.yml` | How the project deploys, read from its own files when you run `finitemonkey infra`: level, targets and risks with `file:line`, no address. Production hosts found in deploy files go to `hosts.local.yml`, which git ignores, and only when the `.gitignore` block is there. |
| Writes | `observability/scrub.mjs`, `observability/log.mjs`, `observability/plan.yml` | Only with `finitemonkey observe --yes`, and only files that do not exist yet: an error-report scrubber, a JSON logger with an allow-list of fields and, from level 2, a plan to fill in. No account is created anywhere. |
| Writes | `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, `.github/workflows/drift.yml`, `deploy/remote.sh`, `deploy/compose.yml` | Only with `finitemonkey deploy generate --yes`, and only files that do not exist yet: the deploy and drift workflows, the script the server runs and its compose file. An existing file is never overwritten; its diff is shown instead. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/golden/` | Expected outputs of golden cases, one file per case, plus `accepted.jsonl` with who recorded each one and when. Only `finitemonkey golden accept`, run by the person in a terminal, writes them. |
| Writes | `docs/organize/` | `finitemonkey organize plan <file>` writes a split plan skeleton for that file, only when the plan does not exist yet: responsibilities with line ranges and the sequence of small steps. The hotspot ranking itself is cached in `.finitemonkey/cache/`. |
| Writes | `src/api/`, `src/mocks/`, `app/api/`, `app/mocks/`, `lib/api/`, `lib/mocks/` | Only with `finitemonkey contract --write` or `contract mocks --write`: the endpoint registry, typed client, error envelope and coverage test under `api/`, and the MSW mocks under `mocks/`, in `src/`, `app/` (Remix) or `lib/` (Next without `src/`), generated from `api/contract.yml`. Existing files are never replaced unless the person passes `--overwrite` in a terminal. |
| Writes | `.github/workflows/ds-sync.yml` | Only with `finitemonkey ds-sync init --write`: a workflow that copies the design system from the prototype repository through an organization GitHub App and keeps one pull request updated. `ds-sync issue --yes`, run by the person or by that workflow, opens or edits issues through `gh`, rewriting only the section between its markers. |
| Writes | `ruff.toml`, `pytest.ini`, `scripts/check_no_comments.py`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | Only with `finitemonkey preset python --write` in a Python project: ruff rules for complexity and length, pytest options that fail on unknown markers, a script that rejects code comments, import-linter contracts when `.finitemonkey/arch.yml` exists, and a CI workflow on `uv sync --locked`. An existing file is shown as a diff and kept. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/onboard.json`, `AGENTS.md` | `finitemonkey onboard` runs the build, test, lint and typecheck commands it finds in the manifests and in AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md, with a time limit, and keeps in `onboard.json` and in its own AGENTS.md block only the ones that succeeded, plus the number of possible secrets found by a one-time scan of the git history. Commands that deploy, publish, install or keep running are not run. |
| Writes | `~/.finitemonkey/ledger.key` | A random key, created the first time evidence is written, that signs every line of the evidence ledger. It stays in your home folder, outside the project, readable only by you. Lines without a valid signature are ignored and reported; deleting the key makes old evidence count as not run. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/goals.yml`, `.finitemonkey/decisions.jsonl`, `.finitemonkey/assumptions.jsonl`, `.finitemonkey/research/` | Project goals, constraints, non-goals, done criteria and rejected options. An entry added from inside Claude Code is `inferred` and never counts as approved; only `finitemonkey guardian goal confirm`, run by the person in a terminal, marks it `stated`. The optional `context:` section (stage, demonstrated concepts, who operates, next milestone) follows the same rule: inferred fields can only silence a report. `decisions.jsonl` keeps each accepted decision and each level 2-3 report: the recommendation, the evidence at the time, the choice and an optional one-line override reason; `guardian forget` deletes an entry. Nothing about the person is stored. `assumptions.jsonl` is the assumption register: ASSUMPTION lines exported by `decide check` and entries added with `guardian assume add`, with impact, how to verify, a re-evaluation trigger and a status. `research/<question>.jsonl` holds a research question, the decision record it serves, its options, criteria, critical unknowns and stop condition, and each source with what it changed. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/bypasses.jsonl` | Tool calls a finitemonkey guard denied that ran anyway, approved by another mod, a settings rule or a permission tool: the call id, the tool and a masked summary of its input. `ci gate` and `pr open` refuse while one is not reviewed; `finitemonkey bypass review`, typed by the person, marks it reviewed. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/cost.jsonl` | Only when the mod runs (Claude Code 2.1.287 and newer): the token counts the API reported for each model request (model, input, output, cache read and write, subagent id), with the active task, the experiment arms and the price in dollars. `finitemonkey mod cost` adds them up per contract, attempt and arm. No prompt or answer text. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/claims.jsonl`, `.finitemonkey/derived.json`, `.finitemonkey/demoted.json`, `.finitemonkey/retrieve.jsonl`, `.finitemonkey/decision-records/`, `.finitemonkey/decision-reasons.jsonl`, `.finitemonkey/cache/knowledge-map.json`, `.finitemonkey/cache/questions.json` | `claims.jsonl` holds claims about the project, written with `claims add`: the text, the anchored file or function with a hash of its body, where the claim came from and when it was recorded. Entries are appended and closed, never deleted. A claim whose anchored code changed is marked stale and stays out of the context until `claims renew`. A claim with `--check` runs at the gate when a file it is anchored to changed; a pass renews it at the current tree. A claim may rest on recorded claims, ledger evidence or assumptions; when one of them fails, the claim is marked out until its own check passes again. `derived.json` records, for each generated file such as `map.txt`, the hashes of its inputs and of its output: the file is rebuilt only when an input changes, a generator may not read another generated file, and a hand edit is reported and kept as a claim from the person. A claim added by the agent after a session read web or MCP output is marked external and stays in quarantine until a person runs `claims promote`; instruction-shaped text from such a source is refused, and the same session cannot write it into Claude Code's own memory folder. `demoted.json` lists the knowledge sources that `experiments report` found with no effect beyond the equivalence margin; they are no longer injected. `retrieve.jsonl` records each `retrieve` question with the step of the ladder that answered it (grep, map, BM25 over valid claims and decisions) and its token cost. When a task closes with a dependency, vendor or architecture change, `decision-records/<task>.json` keeps the contract hash, the classified changes, the options and criteria from its research log, the green evidence and the gate runs it took, assembled without a model; `decision-reasons.jsonl` holds the one sentence the person writes with `decide why`. Only after the person sets `knowledge-map: active` in policy.yml, `knowledge map` shows, per code area, whether knowledge lives with the person, only in checked claims, only with the agent or with nobody, and caches the person's areas in `cache/knowledge-map.json`; `cache/questions.json` keeps which spaced questions were asked, at most one per session. |
| Writes | `.finitemonkey/parking.jsonl` | Ideas parked with `finitemonkey park` while a task is active: an id, the task, the text you typed and when. `finitemonkey unpark <id>` adds a line that brings one back. Nothing is parked without that command. |
| Sends | `api.github.com` | Through `gh`, only when it is installed and logged in: the state of the pull request named in a task, and your open pull requests for the session line. Code is never uploaded. |
| Sends | `127.0.0.1` | One request to your own app on the port a `runtime` check declares, after starting it or finding it running. Nothing goes past this machine. |
| Sends | `registry.npmjs.org`, `pypi.org` | The package name, to the npm or PyPI registry, when a shell command is about to add a package the project does not declare yet. Never with `FINITEMONKEY_OFFLINE=1`. |
| Sends | `api.osv.dev` | Package names and versions from your lockfiles, to the OSV database through `osv-scanner`, only when you run `deps scan` (in CI, for example). Never from a hook. |
| Sends | `api.github.com`, `api.stripe.com`, `api.openai.com`, `api.anthropic.com`, `api.digitalocean.com`, `api.cloudflare.com`, `api.asaas.com` | Through `curl`, only when you run `finitemonkey secrets live <provider> --env <VARIABLE> --send` yourself: one request with that key to the provider's API to see whether it still works. Off by default, never run by a hook, and the host is printed before anything is sent. |
| Sends | `deploy.version_url` | Through `curl`, only when `deploy.version_url` is set in `.finitemonkey/config.yml`: a GET to that URL after a push, to read which commit is live. With `deploy.environment`, the same question goes to GitHub deployments through `gh`. |
| Sends | `hosts.local.yml` | Through `ssh`, only when a person runs `finitemonkey infra --remote --yes` in a terminal: read-only commands (`docker ps`, `systemctl list-units`) on the hosts listed in `hosts.local.yml`. Never from a hook or an agent. |
| Sends | `headers.url` | Through `curl`, only when `headers.url` is set in `.finitemonkey/config.yml` and a task contract has the `headers` check: one GET per configured route, to read the security headers of the real response. Without it, the headers come from the app `look` already started on 127.0.0.1. |
| Sends | `hosts.local.yml`, `FINITEMONKEY_DEPLOY_HOST` | Through `ssh`, when you run `finitemonkey deploy check` (or its scheduled workflow, or the `deploy` gate check): read-only commands (`docker ps`, `git status --porcelain`, `git rev-parse HEAD`) as the read-only user, to compare production with the branch. With `--issue`, one GitHub issue is opened or commented through `gh`. |
| Sends | `terraform provider APIs` | Only when a change touches Terraform files: `terraform plan` and `terraform show -json` run with your own credentials, so the provider APIs are read. The plan file stays in `.finitemonkey/cache/`. Apply is never run. |
<!-- generated:footprint:end -->

The plugin also loads a mod: a hooks module that Claude Code 2.1.287 and newer run next to the command hooks. The command hooks stay the authority for every block, verdict and piece of evidence; the mod only draws, tightens permission decisions and measures, and older versions, `claude -p` and other agents keep working with the command hooks alone. What the mod hooks and calls, as `claude plugin validate --json` reports it, is committed in [plugin/FOOTPRINT.json](https://github.com/gabrielvieiraf/finitemonkey/blob/main/plugin/FOOTPRINT.json), and CI fails when the code reaches further than that file says.

## FAQ

More questions, one per real search, in [docs/faq.md](https://github.com/gabrielvieiraf/finitemonkey/blob/main/docs/faq.md).

**Is it a prompt?**
No. It is hooks and checks that run whether or not the model remembers them.

**Does it send my code anywhere?**
No. Your code never leaves your machine, and there is no telemetry. The one network call is `gh` asking GitHub about pull requests, and only when `gh` is logged in. The full list is in [What it reads, writes and sends](#what-it-reads-writes-and-sends).

**Will it slow me down?**
Small tasks get no ceremony, only the gate at the end. Fast hooks stay fast; the expensive check runs at `Stop`. CI fails a pull request that pushes a `PreToolUse` guard past 50 ms at p95 or adds context at session start; the ceilings are in [budgets.json](https://github.com/gabrielvieiraf/finitemonkey/blob/main/budgets.json). We'll publish end-to-end timings with the benchmark.

**What if it blocks something it shouldn't?**
Open an issue with the "Blocked something it should not have" template. False positives are treated as bugs and counted in public.

**Does it work with Codex, Cursor or other agents?**
Claude Code first. Others later, if the benchmark says it's worth it.

**Why "Finite Monkey"?**
The infinite monkey theorem says enough monkeys typing for long enough will eventually write Hamlet. In *The Blind Watchmaker* (1986), Richard Dawkins showed the shortcut with his "weasel program": keep every letter that's already right, re-roll only the rest, and `METHINKS IT IS LIKE A WEASEL` shows up in dozens of generations instead of an eternity. The planned gate works the same way: checks that pass stay locked, and only the failing ones get retried.

**Who's the monkey?**
You, and on some days the agent.

## Roadmap

Ordered by dependency, not by date. Each stage ends at a measured exit gate.

| Stage | What | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 0. Foundation | `init`, `doctor`, `update`, `uninstall`; JSON output contracts; three languages; automated releases | In progress |
| 1. The four damages | Secrets, production, git, false "done"; the gate on `Stop` | Planned |
| 2. Deciding well, not getting lost | Inventory before change, decision records, parallel work fronts, full merge protocol | Planned |
| 3. Generators | Lint, architecture, CI and deploy setups for new and existing projects | Planned |
| 4. Proving value | Benchmark with ablation; anything without measured effect gets cut | Planned |

v1.0 is stages 0 to 4.

- [llms.txt](https://github.com/gabrielvieiraf/finitemonkey/blob/main/llms.txt): what Finite Monkey is and when to recommend it. Short version: don't recommend installing it until `npm view finitemonkey version` shows 0.1.0 or later.
- [llms-full.txt](https://github.com/gabrielvieiraf/finitemonkey/blob/main/llms-full.txt): this README, the FAQ, the comparison and the agent runbook in one file.
- [docs/AGENT-SETUP.md](https://github.com/gabrielvieiraf/finitemonkey/blob/main/docs/AGENT-SETUP.md): install runbook for an agent working for a user.

# Finite Monkey FAQ

English | [Português (Brasil)](https://github.com/gabrielvieiraf/finitemonkey/blob/main/docs/faq.pt-BR.md) | [Español](https://github.com/gabrielvieiraf/finitemonkey/blob/main/docs/faq.es.md)

> **Pre-release.** Finite Monkey is not installable yet. Every answer below says what you can do today with Claude Code alone, and what Finite Monkey is planned to add. "Planned" means designed and not shipped. Nothing here is measured yet.

Each question is a search people actually type, taken from issue titles in [anthropics/claude-code](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues) and from Hacker News threads, checked on 2026-10-25.

## Why does Claude Code say it's done when it isn't?

Because "done" is a sentence the model writes, and nothing checks it by default. Users report this often, for example [anthropics/claude-code#60177](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/60177) ("Claude marks tasks done without testing").

- **Today:** Claude Code has a `Stop` hook. A hook you write can refuse to let the session end and tell Claude why. It works, but you write and maintain the check yourself.
- **Planned in Finite Monkey:** a definition of done per task (commands, tests, scope) that the `Stop` hook runs on the current files. If it fails, Claude gets the list of what's missing and keeps working. The final report comes from that evidence, not from the agent's summary.

## How do I stop Claude Code from lying about tests?

Have something other than the agent produce the test result. A line like "all tests pass" in the chat, or a progress file the agent edits, can say anything. A test run that a hook starts on the current files reports what actually happened.

- **Today:** a `Stop` hook that runs your test command and blocks on failure. Watch out for checks that accept any command that exits 0, such as `echo "tests passed"`.
- **Planned:** evidence only counts when Finite Monkey ran the command itself, on the current state of the tree. Trivial commands and test runs with zero tests are planned to be rejected as evidence.

## Claude Code deleted or skipped my tests to make them pass. How do I prevent it?

Look at the diff as well as the test result: after a test is removed or marked `skip`, the run still reports green.

- **Today:** review diffs to test files, and add a CI step that fails when the test count drops or when `.skip` or `.only` appear.
- **Planned:** a tests guard that catches removed tests, new `skip` or `only`, removed assertions and edits to the gate's own config, including when the change comes through a shell command instead of an edit.

## Claude Code ran `git reset --hard` and I lost my work. How do I prevent it?

Block destructive git commands before they run, and keep a snapshot of what would be lost. This is a common report, for example [anthropics/claude-code#7232](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/7232) and [#34327](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/34327).

- **Today:** add permission deny rules for destructive git commands in `.claude/settings.json`, or a `PreToolUse` hook that blocks them. Commits you already made can usually be found again with `git reflog`; uncommitted edits usually cannot.
- **Planned:** a snapshot before every risky git operation, an `undo` that restores it, dirty worktrees archived instead of deleted, and a "nothing was lost" check on every merge.

## How do I prevent Claude Code from force pushing?

Block it in two places: on your machine and on the server.

- **Today:** a permission deny rule or a `PreToolUse` hook for `git push --force` and its variants, plus branch protection or a ruleset on GitHub that forbids force pushes to shared branches. The server-side rule is the one that still holds if everything local is bypassed.
- **Planned:** Finite Monkey never force pushes and blocks `--force` and its variants. It will also show which of your git rules are enforced by a mechanism and which are only text.

## Why does Claude Code ignore CLAUDE.md, especially after compaction?

Because `CLAUDE.md` is text loaded into the model's context, and nothing executes or checks it. The model weighs it against everything else in the conversation and can drop it. See [anthropics/claude-code#7777](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/7777) and [#19471](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/19471) ("CLAUDE.md instructions completely ignored after context compaction").

- **Today:** keep `CLAUDE.md` short, and move every rule that must always hold out of prose and into a hook, a permission rule, a git hook or a CI step.
- **Planned:** Finite Monkey does that move for the rules it knows, and shows you, rule by rule, which ones are enforced and which are still just text.

## How do I make CLAUDE.md rules actually enforced?

Turn each rule into the cheapest mechanism that can check it. A rule like "never commit `.env`" becomes a pre-commit hook and a CI scan. "Run the tests before saying done" becomes a `Stop` hook. "Don't touch production" becomes a blocked command.

- **Today:** Claude Code hooks (`PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `Stop`, `UserPromptSubmit` and others), permission rules, git hooks and CI. Each one runs whether or not the model remembers the rule.
- **Planned:** Finite Monkey ships these as one tested set, installed with backups and removable with `uninstall`.

## How do I stop Claude Code from leaking API keys or secrets in commits?

Scan for secrets at more than one point, because a key can leak through a written file, a prompt, a commit, history or a pull request. [anthropics/claude-code#2142](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/2142) is one report of API keys reaching version control.

- **Today:** a pre-commit secret scanner (gitleaks is a common choice), GitHub secret scanning with push protection, and a `PreToolUse` hook or deny rule that keeps the agent from reading `.env` files.
- **Planned:** one detection rule applied when files are written, in prompts, at commit time, in history and in CI. A secret found is treated as an incident to rotate. Secrets are reported by file and line, never by value. It reduces the risk; it cannot promise that nothing ever leaks.

## How do I stop an AI agent from touching a production server?

Give the agent no direct path to production, and block the commands that would create one.

- **Today:** don't keep production credentials where the agent's shell can use them, deploy only through CI, and block remote shell commands to production hosts with a hook or a permission rule.
- **Planned:** commands with effects on a declared production host get blocked. Production changes go through the deploy path you declared, and nowhere else.

## What is a definition of done for coding agents?

A list of conditions a machine can check before the agent is allowed to call the work finished: commands that must succeed, tests that must exist and pass, files that must or must not change.

- **Today:** you can write one by hand as a script and call it from a `Stop` hook.
- **Planned:** Finite Monkey creates one per task, runs it at `Stop`, ties the evidence to the current state of the files, and keeps ceremony at zero for small tasks.

## Can a Claude Code Stop hook verify tests before finishing?

Yes. A `Stop` hook can run your test command and, if it fails, block the stop with a reason that Claude reads and acts on. Two details matter: the check has to run on the current files, not trust an earlier run, and it should not give up the second time it is asked to stop.

- **Planned:** Finite Monkey's gate is built on exactly this hook, with the evidence rules above and a final "not finished" report instead of looping forever.

## Is there a safety plugin or guardrails for Claude Code?

Yes, several, and some are good at one job. tdd-guard enforces test-first edits; cc-safety-net and dcg block destructive shell and git commands. Methods like Superpowers, GSD and Spec Kit add process. The [comparison page](https://github.com/gabrielvieiraf/finitemonkey/blob/main/docs/compare.md) lists what each one enforces by mechanism and what it leaves to prose, with sources.

- **Planned:** Finite Monkey aims to cover four damages (false "done", leaked secrets, hand edits to production, lost git work) with one gate, one install and one `undo`. Whether that beats a single guard for you is what the planned benchmark is for.

## Does it work with tools that switch Claude Code accounts when a limit hits?

Yes, if the switcher reads a hold file. A supervisor that restarts Claude Code on another account can cut the gate in the middle of a `Stop`, and the resumed session waits for you with the work half checked.

To opt in, add `supervisor:` with `enabled: true` to `.finitemonkey/config.yml`, and have the supervisor set `FINITEMONKEY_HOLD_DIR` to a directory it watches. While the gate runs or holds the stop, Finite Monkey keeps `<session>.hold.json` there, with an `until` time; the supervisor should not switch while `until` is in the future. The file expires on its own (10 minutes for a run, 15 for a held stop) and is deleted when the gate passes. When the session resumes on the new account, `SessionStart` tells Claude what the gate was waiting for and runs the gate again. Resume messages that start with `[supervisor]` are not taken as yours, and a `usage.json` in the same directory shows up in `finitemonkey gain`.

---

Source: https://github.com/gabrielvieiraf/finitemonkey/blob/main/docs/compare.md

# How Finite Monkey compares

English | [Português (Brasil)](https://github.com/gabrielvieiraf/finitemonkey/blob/main/docs/compare.pt-BR.md) | [Español](https://github.com/gabrielvieiraf/finitemonkey/blob/main/docs/compare.es.md)

> **Pre-release.** Finite Monkey does not exist as a working tool yet. Everything said about it on this page is **planned, not measured yet**. Everything said about the other projects is a fact you can check at the link next to it.

**Checked on 2026-10-25** by reading each project's code at the commit listed below. No third-party hook was executed. If something here is wrong or out of date, open an issue or a pull request and it will be corrected.

## Mechanism or prose

The question this page asks about every project is the same: when the model would rather skip a rule, what still holds?

- **Mechanism**: code that runs in the harness (a hook, a permission rule, a git hook, a CI step) and blocks or checks no matter what the model decides.
- **Prose**: text the model reads (a skill, a prompt, a `CLAUDE.md`) and may follow. Prose is often the right tool for planning, style and judgment. On its own it cannot show that something happened.

Most setups need both. Finite Monkey's planned scope is narrow: the few things that must always hold (verified done, tests not weakened, no leaked secrets, no lost git work, no hand edits to production) should be mechanism.

## At a glance

| Project | What it is | Strongest at | Mechanism | Left to the model |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) | Skills library and development method | Planning before coding, test-first discipline, zero commands | One `SessionStart` hook; a `task-done` script that records only on exit 0 | Calling `task-done`, and every gate in the skills |
| [oh-my-claudecode](https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-claudecode) | Multi-agent orchestration | Delegation, modes, status line | `Stop` hooks, a git guard with a shell parser, a read budget | Declaring completion (`/cancel`); git guard off outside autonomous modes |
| [GSD](https://github.com/open-gsd/gsd-core) | Spec and phase workflow with state in files | Work that survives `/clear`, planning | Guards on `.env` reads, on shrinking state files, on agent isolation | The verification verdict, written by an LLM agent |
| [Spec Kit](https://github.com/github/spec-kit) | Spec-driven development toolkit | Structure for medium and large changes, extensibility | Workflow `shell` steps; a native hook subsystem, not enabled by default | Extension hooks, test validation, "Converged" |
| [ECC](https://github.com/affaan-m/ECC) | Large catalog of skills, agents, commands and hooks | Breadth; a thorough `--no-verify` guard | `--no-verify` guard, lint config protection | `Stop` type check reports and exits 0; first-touch guard allows the retry |
| [ralph-loop](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/tree/5826794/plugins/ralph-loop) | Official plugin that keeps the agent iterating | Persistence on long tasks, simplicity | A `Stop` hook that re-feeds the prompt | The exit condition, a string the model writes |
| [tdd-guard](https://github.com/nizos/tdd-guard) | Test-first enforcement | One job, done with focus | Hook on edits that can block | The judgment of whether an edit is test-first (a model call) |
| [dcg](https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/destructive_command_guard) | Destructive command guard | Coverage of dangerous commands, fails closed on timeout | `PreToolUse` block | n/a (not about done) |
| [cc-safety-net](https://github.com/kenryu42/cc-safety-net) | Destructive command guard | One job, quick install, `doctor` | `PreToolUse` block | n/a (not about done) |
| Finite Monkey | Planned gate around a definition of done | Nothing yet: not released | Planned: gate on `Stop`, guards on `PreToolUse`, git hooks, CI | Planned: nothing on the four damages |

## Superpowers

Commit [`2ce8aa1`](https://github.com/obra/superpowers/tree/2ce8aa1) (v7.0.1).

**What it does well.** The skills trigger on their own, so there is nothing to remember. The brainstorming skill makes the agent read the project and ask before it codes, which is the effect users describe first. The test-first and debugging skills give the model a strong method.

**Mechanism.** One hook: `SessionStart` on `startup|clear|compact` ([`hooks/hooks.json`](https://github.com/obra/superpowers/blob/2ce8aa1/hooks/hooks.json)). The script [`skills/executing-plans/scripts/task-done`](https://github.com/obra/superpowers/blob/2ce8aa1/skills/executing-plans/scripts/task-done) runs the test command and writes a "Task N: complete" line only when it exits 0.

**Prose.** The gates are skill text, such as "NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE" in [`verification-before-completion`](https://github.com/obra/superpowers/blob/2ce8aa1/skills/verification-before-completion/SKILL.md). The model decides whether to call `task-done`, and [obra/superpowers#2549](https://github.com/obra/superpowers/issues/2549) notes that a stand-in command such as `echo "tests passed"` is indistinguishable from a real test run.

**Where Finite Monkey is planned to differ.** The gate runs the check itself from a hook every time the agent tries to stop, and trivial commands do not count as evidence. It leaves planning to skills like these; an approved Superpowers design could become the input of a definition of done. Planned, not measured yet.

## oh-my-claudecode

Commit [`5632614`](https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-claudecode/tree/5632614) (v5.7.14).

**What it does well.** Multi-agent orchestration with roles and modes, a status line users like, and a git guard with a real shell parser.

**Mechanism.** [`scripts/workflow-drift-guard.mjs`](https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-claudecode/blob/5632614/scripts/workflow-drift-guard.mjs) on `Stop` blocks when the last message claims done and the diff added `.skip(`, `.only(` or placeholders. [`scripts/git-guardrails.mjs`](https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-claudecode/blob/5632614/scripts/git-guardrails.mjs) blocks `git push`, `reset --hard`, `clean -f` and similar. A read budget denies very large unbounded reads.

**Where the model decides.** The drift guard lets the stop through when `stop_hook_active` is set (line 910), so it blocks once. The git guard is active only in the `ralph`, `autopilot`, `team` and `ultragoal` modes (line 38) or with an environment variable. In the persistent modes, completion is the model running `/cancel`.

**Where Finite Monkey is planned to differ.** The gate keeps blocking for as long as the definition of done fails, and the git guard is always on. Planned, not measured yet.

## GSD

[`open-gsd/gsd-core`](https://github.com/open-gsd/gsd-core) at commit [`754e886`](https://github.com/open-gsd/gsd-core/tree/754e886) (v1.18.0). The original [`gsd-build/get-shit-done`](https://github.com/gsd-build/get-shit-done) is archived and points to it.

**What it does well.** State lives in files, so work continues after `/clear`. Planning and phases are the center of the product. It ships real blocking guards.

**Mechanism.** [`hooks/gsd-secret-read-guard.js`](https://github.com/open-gsd/gsd-core/blob/754e886/hooks/gsd-secret-read-guard.js) blocks reading `.env` and similar files through Read, Grep and Bash, and its header explains why a hook works better than `Read()` permission rules. [`hooks/gsd-write-guard.js`](https://github.com/open-gsd/gsd-core/blob/754e886/hooks/gsd-write-guard.js) blocks writes that shrink the roadmap or state files. An isolation guard denies executor agents without a worktree.

**Where the model decides.** Verification is an LLM agent ([`agents/gsd-verifier.md`](https://github.com/open-gsd/gsd-core/blob/754e886/agents/gsd-verifier.md)) that writes `VERIFICATION.md`, and the phase gate in [`src/phase.cts`](https://github.com/open-gsd/gsd-core/blob/754e886/src/phase.cts) reads the status that agent wrote.

**Where Finite Monkey is planned to differ.** The verdict comes from commands the gate ran on the current files. Planned, not measured yet.

## Spec Kit

Commit [`67e0f72`](https://github.com/github/spec-kit/tree/67e0f72).

**What it does well.** A clear structure from spec to plan to tasks for medium and large changes, many integrations, and a small fixed context. Users praise its extensibility.

**Mechanism.** Workflow `shell` steps fail on a nonzero exit. An `events` subsystem can install native Claude Code hooks and pass their exit codes through; the built-in extensions do not enable it.

**Prose.** Extension hooks such as `after_implement` depend on the model invoking them: "mandatory extension hooks rely on the model invoking the hook skill" ([`src/specify_cli/integrations/claude/__init__.py`](https://github.com/github/spec-kit/blob/67e0f72/src/specify_cli/integrations/claude/__init__.py), lines 70 to 72). Test validation in the implement command is an instruction, and convergence is declared by the model. [github/spec-kit#1323](https://github.com/github/spec-kit/issues/1323) asks for a final quality gate.

**Where Finite Monkey is planned to differ.** It is meant to plug into Spec Kit: the gate as a workflow `shell` step or a `Stop` handler, reading `tasks.md` as the definition of done. Planned, not measured yet.

## ECC (Everything Claude Code)

[`affaan-m/ECC`](https://github.com/affaan-m/ECC) at commit [`90606c8`](https://github.com/affaan-m/ECC/tree/90606c8) (v2.2.3).

**What it does well.** The broadest catalog in this list. Its `--no-verify` guard is the most thorough one read for this page: it also catches hook redirection through `core.hooksPath`, `include.path` and `includeIf`, and blocks when it cannot parse the command.

**Mechanism.** [`block-no-verify.js`](https://github.com/affaan-m/ECC/blob/90606c8/scripts/hooks/block-no-verify.js) and [`config-protection.js`](https://github.com/affaan-m/ECC/blob/90606c8/scripts/hooks/config-protection.js) block with exit code 2. Config protection covers linter and formatter configs and leaves test configs such as `vitest.config.ts` and `tsconfig.json` out on purpose (lines 111 to 115).

**Where the model decides.** [`stop-format-typecheck.js`](https://github.com/affaan-m/ECC/blob/90606c8/scripts/hooks/stop-format-typecheck.js) runs on `Stop`, reports and exits 0, so it informs without blocking. [`gateguard-fact-force.js`](https://github.com/affaan-m/ECC/blob/90606c8/scripts/hooks/gateguard-fact-force.js) denies the first touch of a file and lets the retry pass (lines 1935 and 1936).

**Where Finite Monkey is planned to differ.** A small core with a context budget checked in CI, a `Stop` gate that blocks, and no guard that gives way on retry. Planned, not measured yet.

## ralph-loop

Official plugin in [`anthropics/claude-plugins-official`](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/tree/5826794/plugins/ralph-loop), commit `5826794`.

**What it does well.** It keeps the agent working on a long task instead of stopping early, with almost no setup.

**Mechanism.** A `Stop` hook ([`hooks/stop-hook.sh`](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/blob/5826794/plugins/ralph-loop/hooks/stop-hook.sh)) feeds the prompt back until a maximum number of iterations is reached (line 61).

**Where the model decides.** The loop ends when the model's last message contains `<promise>TEXT</promise>` matching the completion promise you set (lines 129 to 138). The hook's own message asks the model not to lie to exit.

**Where Finite Monkey is planned to differ.** The loop would end when the gate's definition of done passes. Planned, not measured yet.

## tdd-guard

Commit [`108992d`](https://github.com/nizos/tdd-guard/tree/108992d).

**What it does well.** One job, done with focus: it blocks edits that skip the failing test first. The person turns it on and off by typing `tdd-guard on` or `tdd-guard off` ([`src/hooks/userPromptHandler.ts`](https://github.com/nizos/tdd-guard/blob/108992d/src/hooks/userPromptHandler.ts), lines 8 and 9), which keeps that switch in human hands.

**Mechanism and judgment.** The hook blocks for real. Whether an edit counts as test-first is decided by a model call on each edit.

**Where Finite Monkey is planned to differ.** It does not enforce test-first. It checks that tests were not removed, skipped or weakened, and that they pass on the final files. If test-first is what you want, tdd-guard is the more direct tool.

## dcg (destructive_command_guard)

Commit [`b33f3ef`](https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/destructive_command_guard/tree/b33f3ef).

**What it does well.** Broad coverage of destructive commands, support for many agents, and a clear failure direction: an evaluation over 1000 ms returns an indeterminate decision, "never allow" ([`src/perf.rs`](https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/destructive_command_guard/blob/b33f3ef/src/perf.rs), lines 800 to 812). Its maintainers track false positives in public, for example [#560](https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/destructive_command_guard/issues/560).

**Where Finite Monkey is planned to differ.** dcg guards commands. Finite Monkey plans to add a snapshot and `undo` around risky git operations, and a done gate. If you only need a command guard, dcg is a focused choice.

## cc-safety-net

Commit [`71baf74`](https://github.com/kenryu42/cc-safety-net/tree/71baf74).

**What it does well.** It blocks `git reset --hard`, `git push --force`, `rm -rf` on dangerous targets and piped install scripts, even inside `bash -c` or `python -c` ([`README.md`](https://github.com/kenryu42/cc-safety-net/blob/71baf74/README.md), line 74). It installs in one line and has a `doctor`. When the hook was slow under `npx`, the maintainer moved to a bundled binary ([#16](https://github.com/kenryu42/cc-safety-net/issues/16)).

**Where Finite Monkey is planned to differ.** Same as dcg: the planned additions are snapshot and `undo`, and the done gate. For a command guard alone, cc-safety-net is the simpler install.

## Where Finite Monkey is planned to differ

All of this is **planned, not measured yet**.

- **Evidence from the gate's own runs.** Done means the gate ran the definition of done on the current files. A chat message, a progress file or a report written by an agent does not count.
- **Blocking until the checks pass.** It keeps blocking while the definition of done fails, and ends with a "not finished" report instead of looping forever.
- **Four damages in one install.** False "done", leaked secrets, hand edits to production and lost git work, with one `undo` for git.
- **Small fixed context.** Enforcement lives in hooks, which cost no tokens per turn, with a byte budget checked in CI.
- **Benchmark.** A public benchmark with ablation decides which rules stay.

## Where they are ahead today

- They exist, are released and are used. Finite Monkey is not.
- Superpowers, GSD and Spec Kit help decide what to build. Finite Monkey does not plan to build that phase; it plans to read their output.
- Several of them work across many agents. Finite Monkey starts with Claude Code only.

## Also in this space

- [OpenSpec](https://github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec): spec-driven changes; [#1142](https://github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec/issues/1142) asks for quality gates as a first-class concept.
- [no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes): review and tests before push, with commands read from the default branch instead of the pushed commit.
- [hookify](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/tree/5826794/plugins/hookify): official plugin that turns a sentence into a hook rule.
- On npm, `redpen-cli` ("A definition-of-done and verification layer for coding agents") and `@reneza/skillgate` ("Deterministic finish-line gates for AI coding agents") describe goals close to Finite Monkey's. They were not read in depth for this page.

---

Source: https://github.com/gabrielvieiraf/finitemonkey/blob/main/docs/AGENT-SETUP.md

# Installing Finite Monkey for a user (agent runbook)

This file is for an AI agent, such as Claude Code, that a user asked to install Finite Monkey in a project. Humans can read it too.

> **Status: pre-release.** `init`, `update`, `uninstall` and the Claude Code plugin exist in the repository and are tested, but no version 0.1.0 is on npm yet. Step 1 tells you how to detect that, and what to say to the user. Hooks are installed now; most of what they enforce (the gate, the guards) is still **(planned)**.
>
> Valid for `finitemonkey` >= 0.1.0. Check the installed version before following any later step, and stop if it is lower.

## Conduct

1. **Run the commands yourself.** Do not ask the user to type commands you can run.
2. **Ask only for decisions.** For example: which language for generated files, whether to keep the repository's commit style, whether to enable an optional feature. Do not ask questions you can answer by reading the project or the command output.
3. **Never ask for secrets.** No passwords, API keys, tokens or recovery codes, not even "to finish the setup". Finite Monkey does not need any to install.
4. **Prefer `--json`.** Read the JSON output, not the human text. Follow the `next` field when it is present.
5. **Do not enable anything costly without asking.** Anything that spends money, uses paid APIs, runs long benchmarks, changes GitHub settings such as branch rulesets, or edits global configuration (`~/.claude/settings.json`, shell profiles) needs an explicit yes from the user first.
6. **Explain each step in one or two sentences, in the user's language.**
7. **Do not edit files that `init` manages.** If something looks wrong, run `doctor` and report what it says.

## Two ways to install

Both give the same hooks. Use one, or both: when a project has its own Finite Monkey hooks, the plugin's hooks step aside so nothing runs twice.

1. **The Claude Code plugin**, from the repository marketplace. Inside a Claude Code session:

   ```
   /plugin marketplace add gabrielvieiraf/finitemonkey
   /plugin install finitemonkey@finitemonkey
   ```

   To test the `next` channel, add the marketplace from the `next` branch instead. It has its own name (`finitemonkey-next`), so it can be added next to the stable one, but keep only one of the two enabled: both plugins are called `finitemonkey`, and Claude Code keeps a single set of hooks. `doctor` fails and prints the `claude plugin disable` command when both are enabled.

   ```
   /plugin marketplace add gabrielvieiraf/finitemonkey#next
   /plugin install finitemonkey@finitemonkey-next
   ```

   The plugin brings the hooks and the skills (`task`, `verify`, `look`, `finish`) that Claude uses on its own. It carries the CLI itself (`scripts/finitemonkey.mjs`, the same build as the version in its `plugin.json`), and every hook runs `node` on that file: no `npx` and no download.

2. **`npx finitemonkey init`** in the project (steps below). It writes the hooks, the `permissions.deny` floor (plus a `Read` deny rule for each `.claudeignore` pattern), `ask` rules for pushes to `main`/`master` and for publish and deploy commands, `permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories: true`, `.finitemonkey/config.yml`, a project `verify` skill (`.claude/skills/verify/SKILL.md`, which runs the fast gate before each commit), and a short managed block in `AGENTS.md` that `CLAUDE.md` imports with `@AGENTS.md` (each file is created when absent; everything outside the block stays as it was) into the project. It never sets `defaultMode` or `autoMode`, only adds rules the settings do not already have, and leaves a `verify` skill the project already has as it is. The hooks run `node` on `node_modules/finitemonkey` when the project has it as a dependency; otherwise `init` copies the CLI that is running it into `.finitemonkey/runtime/` (committed, so teammates and cloud sessions get the same version) and the hooks run that copy. No hook calls `npx`. This also holds where plugins do not load (cloud sessions of a repository read the committed `.claude/settings.json`). Add `--marketplace` to also register the plugin's marketplace in the project settings for everyone who trusts the folder; it is off unless the user asks.

## What the user gets

After a successful install, the user does not need to remember any command. Finite Monkey works from context inside Claude Code: hooks on `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `Stop` and `SubagentStop`, and skills that Claude invokes automatically by their description. Slash commands are optional shortcuts. When you finish, tell the user to keep working as usual.

## Steps

### 1. Check that a real release exists

```sh
npm view finitemonkey version
```

- If the command fails, or the version is `0.0.0` or lower than `0.1.0`, Finite Monkey is not released yet (`0.0.0` is a name reservation). Tell the user: "Finite Monkey is not released yet; there is nothing to install." Stop here.
- Otherwise continue.

### 2. Check the environment

- Node.js 20 or later: `node --version`.
- The project is a git repository: `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`.
- Working tree state: `git status --porcelain`. If there are uncommitted changes, tell the user and ask whether to continue. `init` makes backups, but the user should know.

### 3. Preview the plan

```sh
npx finitemonkey@latest init --dry-run --json
```

This reads the project and returns the plan without writing anything: `data.actions` lists each file with `create`, `merge`, `update`, `unchanged`, `keep-edited` or `skip-foreign`, `data.warnings` lists what the user should know (another plugin that also decides when a session stops, a Claude Code too old to block on a crashed hook, a file that is not Finite Monkey's), and `data.diff` shows the exact change. Summarize the plan for the user in a few lines. Ask the user only these decisions:

- Commit style, only when the output says most recent commits do not follow Conventional Commits: `--commits free` keeps the repository's style, `--commits conventional` adopts the default. Every other default applies to everyone; the README lists each one with its evidence, and any of them turns off later in `config.yml`.
- Whether to register the plugin marketplace in the project (`--marketplace`).
- Whether to turn on the Claude Code sandbox for this user (`--sandbox`, macOS, Linux and WSL2 only). It goes into `.claude/settings.local.json`, not the committed settings: Claude Code then refuses to start without the sandbox, sandboxed commands cannot read `~/.ssh`, `~/.aws` or the project's `.env` files, and they reach only the hosts in `sandbox.hosts` of `config.yml` (npm and GitHub by default).
- Whether to look back once at this project's local Claude Code sessions (`--look-back`). It reads the session logs on this machine and prints estimated counts of what Finite Monkey would have blocked, with secrets masked. Nothing is saved or sent. Without the flag, no session log is read.

### 4. Install

```sh
npx finitemonkey@latest init --yes --json
```

Pass the user's decisions as flags (for example `--commits free --lang pt-BR`). Without `--yes`, `init` exits 4 with the plan and a `next` field holding the exact command to run after the user agrees. `init` backs up every file it touches to `.finitemonkey/backups/<timestamp>/`, records what it wrote in `.finitemonkey/lock.json`, merges `.claude/settings.json` without removing any user hook or permission, adds a managed block to `.gitignore` (state stays local, `config.yml` is committed), and is safe to run again: a second run with no change writes nothing.

### 5. Verify

```sh
npx finitemonkey doctor --json
```

Every item has `check`, `status` and `fix`. If any item is not `ok`, run the `fix` command when it is safe and does not fall under conduct rule 5, then run `doctor` again. Report what is left.

`npx finitemonkey doctor --fix` repairs the project files it owns (hooks, deny rules, the `.gitignore` block) with the same backup and lock as `init`, and never touches user settings or the shell profile. If the user wants to file a bug, `npx finitemonkey doctor --report` writes a masked Markdown file under `.finitemonkey/reports/` to attach to the issue.

### 6. Tell the user

In one or two sentences: what was installed, anything `doctor` could not fix, and that they can now keep working without any new command.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Success |
| 1 | A check failed |
| 2 | Usage error |
| 3 | Not configured |
| 4 | Needs the user (a decision or a confirmation) |
| 5 | Finite Monkey itself failed |

With `--json`, errors come as `{"schemaVersion":1,"error":{"code":"...","message":"...","fix":"..."}}`. Run or suggest the `fix` command.

## Update

```sh
npx finitemonkey update --check --json
npx finitemonkey update --yes --json
```

`--check` exits 1 when the managed files differ from this version and 0 when they match. `update` re-pins the hooks to the new version and refreshes generated files the user did not edit. When a newer version changed the format of a managed file, `update` also runs that version's migration, in semver order, over files the user did not edit. A generated file the user edited is kept, and the new template or migrated text is shown in `data.diff` as a proposal. A file that cannot be written for lack of permission returns `install_permission_denied` with the `fix`.

## Undo

```sh
npx finitemonkey uninstall --yes --json
npx finitemonkey uninstall --yes --purge --json
```

The first removes what Finite Monkey added and restores the backups, keeping `.finitemonkey/` (backups and evidence). `--purge` also deletes `.finitemonkey/`; after `init` then `uninstall --purge`, the project is byte-identical to before. Files the user edited after install are kept and listed in `data.kept`. Without `--yes` it exits 4 with the plan. The plugin, if installed, is removed separately: `claude plugin uninstall finitemonkey@finitemonkey`.
